text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clocks service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- Clients withdrdew HUF 21 billion from Friday morning to Sunday afternoon following rumours that Postabank is going to bankrupt. Finance Ministry state secretary Laszlo Akar, suggesting that political considerations may be behind the rush on deposits, said the secret service will uncover the origins of the rumours.

- Demonstrating farmers at Kiskoros established a new interest body Friday and said they regard a government proposal outlined in a letter from Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy as a basis for negotiations. @
- The Democratic Forum's national convention decided to conclude an election agreement with the Young Democrats and the Christian Democrats before late May.

- Hungary's arguments will be heard first in the Hague today when the trial on the Gabcikovo hydropower plant and Slovakia's unilateral diversion of the Danube starts at the International Court of Justice.

- On Saturday visiting Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov discussed European integration processes, his country's intention to join CEFTA and grain deals, but Bulgaria is beset by major payment problems. @
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Moldova's Privatisation Minister Ceslav Coiorbanu visited Budapest Friday to study Hungarian privatisation techniques.

- The Swedish Saab consortium and British Aerospace are offering long-term preferential terms of payment, job creation investment projects and industrial development to Hungary if it decides to upgrade its air force with JAS-39 Gripen fighters.
- Budapest City Council approved the privatisation strategy of the heading company Fotav at its Friday meeting. @
- The traditional china manufacturer Herendi generated a HUF 1.12 billion profit last year, on revenues of HUF 4.5 billion.
- The insurance concern Providencia Rt. increased its revenues by 31 percent to HUF 17.75 billion in 1996. (Sat.)

- The price of Postabank shares on Budapest's OTC market plunged from the usual 70 percent of face value to just 5-10 percent on Friday, in the wake of panic withdrawals brought on by rumours of the bank's insolvency. (Sat.)
VILAGGAZDASAG @
- Meat processing companies will increase their prices by 18-20 percent today or a week from now.
- Hungarian investors sent half of their $66 million abroad last year, including contributions in kind, to Great Britain's tax haven, the Island of Jersey.
- The distribution of shares in the Budapest electricity works Elmu Rt. left a surprisingly high HUF 2.8 billion worth available to secondary holders of compensation coupons.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @

- The National Consumer Protection Society and the Hungarian Automobile Club have filed a complaint with the Economic Competition Agency against Elmka, the company running the 42-km stretch of the M1 toll highway, alleging that Elmka is misleading motorists.
- Budapest Mayor Gabor Demszky and Zoran Djindjic, the new Mayor of Belgrade, signed a statement of intent on co-operation in Belgrade.
